Compute the barcode metrics

Source: R/compute_metrics.R
compute_metrics.Rd

Computes, for each barcode, the log2 fold change between the treated and the control samples of a given time point, and its Z-score and robust Z-score. The result is the input of the Z-score methods (find_gene_zscore_hit, find_zscore_hit) and of several plots. More information about the Z-score and other metrics used in genetic screens can be found in this paper.

Usage

compute_metrics(screenR_Object, control, treatment, day, pseudocount = 0.5)

Arguments

screenR_Object

The ScreenR object obtained using create_screenr_object.

control

The value(s) of the Treatment column of the data table (see get_sample_table) that identify the control samples.

treatment

The value(s) of the Treatment column of the data table that identify the treated samples.

day

The day (time point) to use, as in the Day column of the data table.

pseudocount

A small value (in counts per million) added to the treated and control mean frequencies before computing the log2 fold change, so that barcodes with zero reads get a finite fold change: Log2FC = log2((Treated + pseudocount) / (Control + pseudocount)). Default 0.5. Barcodes with zero reads in both treated and control are removed. The value is on the scale of the normalized count table, which is counts per million of all the reads for the "cpm" and "tmm" methods of normalize_data, but per million reads of the control barcodes for the "control" method.

Value

A tibble with one row for each barcode and the columns Barcode, Gene, Treated and Control (the mean normalized counts), Log2FC, Zscore, ZscoreRobust, Day and Treatment.

Details

The function uses the data table, so run normalize_data and compute_data_table first. For each barcode the normalized counts of the treated and of the control samples of the given day are averaged, then Log2FC = log2((Treated + pseudocount) / (Control + pseudocount)), Zscore = (Log2FC - mean(Log2FC)) / sd(Log2FC) and ZscoreRobust = (Log2FC - median(Log2FC)) / mad(Log2FC), where the mean, standard deviation, median and median absolute deviation are computed over all the barcodes. Since the replicates are averaged, their variability is not used: see compute_barcode_statistics for a replicate-aware alternative.

See also

find_gene_zscore_hit, compute_barcode_statistics, find_discordant_barcodes, plot_zscore_distribution, plot_barcode_trend

Examples

object <- get0("object", envir = asNamespace("ScreenR"))
metrics <- compute_metrics(object,
    control = "Time3",
    treatment = "TRT", day = "Time3"
)
head(metrics)
